_comment: Dynamically-confirmed / strongly-supported stellar-mass black hole X-ray binaries, curated from the BlackCAT catalog of Galactic black holes (Corral-Santana et al. 2016, A&A 587, A61, https://www.astro.puc.cl/BlackCAT/) plus subsequent literature. Coordinates are ICRS J2000 decimal degrees. Masses/distances with significant disagreement across the literature are marked approx:true. 'confirmed' objects have a robust dynamical (radial-velocity) mass function placing the compact object above the neutron-star limit; 'candidate' objects are classified as black holes from X-ray spectral/timing behavior alone, without a secure dynamical mass.

objects.name: Cygnus X-1
objects.notes: First widely accepted stellar-mass black hole, identified 1971-72.
objects.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021, Science 371, 1046 (VLBI parallax + dynamical mass)

objects.name: V404 Cygni
objects.notes: Famous 1989 and 2015 outbursts; mass estimates in literature range ~6.4-12 Msun.
objects.source: Khargharia et al. 2010, ApJ 716, 1105; Miller-Jones et al. 2009 (parallax)

objects.name: GRO J1655-40
objects.notes: Displayed superluminal radio jets in 1994-95.
objects.source: Corral-Santana et al. 2016 BlackCAT; Beer & Podsiadlowski 2002

objects.name: A0620-00
objects.notes: Closest known stellar-mass black hole to Earth.

objects.name: GX 339-4
objects.notes: One of the most active Galactic BH transients; inclination poorly known so mass is loosely constrained (~5.8-10 Msun).

objects.name: XTE J1550-564
objects.notes: Showed relativistic jets and X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations.

objects.name: GS 2000+25
objects.notes: 1988 X-ray nova.

objects.name: GRS 1124-683
objects.notes: One of the earliest hard X-ray/gamma-ray detected BH novae.

objects.name: 4U 1543-475
objects.notes: Unusually early-type (A-star) donor.

objects.name: XTE J1859+226
objects.notes: 1999-2000 X-ray nova with superhump periodicity.

objects.name: GRS 1915+105
objects.notes: Persistently active since 1992; famous for superluminal jets and extreme QPO behavior.

objects.name: H1705-250
objects.notes: One of the first soft X-ray transients recognized as a BH candidate.

objects.name: XTE J1650-500
objects.notes: Originally reported as one of the lowest-mass BH candidates; later work disputes the mass function, so the BH classification itself is debated.
objects.source: Orosz et al. 2004, ApJ 616, 376; Corral-Santana et al. 2016 BlackCAT

objects.name: XTE J1118+480
objects.notes: Unusual high-Galactic-latitude location, possibly a halo/thick-disk object.

objects.name: MAXI J1836-194
objects.notes: Classified BH candidate from X-ray spectral state, no secure dynamical mass yet measured.

objects.name: Swift J1753.5-0127
objects.notes: Unusually compact orbit (~3.2 hr) for its outburst history; distance disputed between ~3 kpc and ~8 kpc.
objects.source: Corral-Santana et al. 2016 BlackCAT; Neustroev et al. 2014

objects.name: MAXI J1305-704
objects.notes: 2012 X-ray nova in a high-inclination system.

objects.name: GS 1354-64
objects.notes: High mass function; distance and hence absolute parameters remain uncertain.

objects.name: MAXI J1659-152
objects.companion: M-dwarf (shortest known BH-XRB orbital period, ~2.4 hr)
objects.notes: Mass estimate is close to the neutron-star/black-hole boundary; classification as a BH is debated.

objects.name: Swift J1357.2-0933
objects.notes: Nicknamed the 'Nightmare' black hole; shows extreme, rapid optical dips.
objects.source: Corral-Santana et al. 2016 BlackCAT; Torres et al. 2015

objects.name: IGR J17091-3624
objects.notes: Nicknamed 'mini GRS 1915+105' for similar variability patterns at lower luminosity; no secure dynamical mass.

objects.name: MAXI J1820+070
objects.notes: One of the brightest X-ray transients of the last decades (2018 outburst).
objects.source: Torres et al. 2020, ApJ 893, L37; Atri et al. 2020 (Gaia parallax)

objects.name: V4641 Sgr
objects.notes: Distance and mass have been substantially revised by Gaia-era studies; older literature used ~9.6 kpc.

objects.name: GRO J0422+32
objects.notes: One of the lowest black-hole mass estimates known, sitting near the putative neutron-star/black-hole mass gap.
objects.source: Casares et al. 2020, MNRAS (mass-gap discussion); Corral-Santana et al. 2016 BlackCAT

objects.name: 4U 1630-47
objects.companion: Unknown (heavily extincted, no optical counterpart identified)
objects.notes: Recurrent transient classified as a BH from X-ray spectral/timing state alone; no mass function exists.

objects.name: GRS 1739-278
objects.notes: Classified BH candidate from X-ray outburst spectral evolution.

objects.name: GRS 1009-45
objects.notes: Mass function of 3.17 Msun implies a black hole for any plausible inclination/mass ratio.

objects.name: 4U 1957+115
objects.notes: Persistently in a soft X-ray state resembling accreting black holes; dynamical mass is very poorly constrained (estimates span roughly 3-17 Msun).
